data.text:
ICYMI O/N

MACRO:

Equities across Asian emerging markets suffered their steepest drop in weeks on Wednesday, with South Korea's benchmark gauge slumpingmore than 6%, as fears over stretched valuations eroded investors' risk appetites. The MSCI index of emerging Asia equities shed 2.6% in its worst intraday decline since the early April "Liberation Day" tariff turmoil. (RTRS)

Democrats swept a trio of races on Tuesday in the first major elections since Donald Trump regained the presidency, elevating a new generation of leaders and giving the beleaguered party a shot of momentum ahead of next year's congressional elections. Democratic socialist Mamdani triumphs in New York mayoral race, while Democrats also won governor races in Virginia and New Jersey. (RTRS)

The Chinese government has issued guidance requiring new data centre projects that have received any state funds to only use domestically-made artificial intelligence chips, according to Reuters sources. (RTRS)

China will continue to suspend its 24% tariffs on some US goods from 1.01 p.m on Nov. 10 for one year while keeping the 10% tariffs, the Ministry of Finance said in announcing the effective date of the previously announced steps. China will also remove retaliatory tariffs that it imposed on a range of US agricultural products such as soybeans and other US agricultural products including corn, wheat, sorghum and chicken. The move was previously flagged in a White House fact sheet. (BBG)

US President Donald Trump announced a cut to fentanyl-related tariffs on imports from China and the continued freeze of some of his reciprocal levies on Chinese goods, formalizing key elements of the sweeping trade deal struck with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. (BBG)

Trump said he met with representatives from Switzerland and announced additional trade talks, as the European nation seeks to reduce a tariff rate that ranks higher than any other developed nation. (BBG)

Major automakers including Tesla, Toyota and Ford, urged the Trump administration on Tuesday to extend a North American free trade deal (USMCA) they call crucial to American auto production. (RTRS)

Republican and Democratic senators signaled optimism about reaching a bipartisan deal to end the government shutdown, while striking cautionary notes about how quickly lawmakers could resolve the impasse. (WSJ)

Traders are increasingly turning to US interest-rate futures where they are wagering on changes between repo rates and the federal funds rate as money-market stress persists. (BBG)

'Global Funds Add to Warnings of Risks in Private Credit' BBG article notes more senior financiers are joining a growing chorus warning of cracks in private credit. (BBG)

The Retail Favorites Index — a Goldman Sachs Group Inc. basket of stocks heavily owned by non-professional traders — saw its largest decline since April 10th on Tuesday. (BBG)

Long-time Bitcoin holders have offloaded around 400,000 Bitcoin over the past month, an exodus of about $45 billion that’s left the market unbalanced. (BBG)

China's services activity expanded in October but at its slowest pace in three months, as a decline in overseas orders offset the boost from improved domestic demand, the RatingDog China General Services PMI showed. (RTRS)

This contrasted slightly with the government's official PMI released on Monday, which rose to 50.2 from 50.1 in September, reflecting differences in sample coverage.

China’s Commerce Ministry is on its biggest public hiring spree this decade, bolstering the unit overseeing rare-earth curbs even as it pauses sweeping measures in a trade truce with the US. (BBG)

Chinese Premier Li Qiang has pledged to further open the country's vast consumer market to international businesses after Beijing and Washington reached a significant trade deal. (BBG)

Chinese Premier Li Qiang said that China's economy will exceed 170 trillion yuan ($23.87 trillion) by 2030, presenting a big market opportunity for the world as trade restrictions rise globally. China has said its GDP will top 140 trillion yuan this year, and the projection by 2030 is in line with proposals for its upcoming five-year plan that predicted annual growth of 4.17% over the next five years. (RTRS)

China’s decision to expand the pilot areas for pension wealth management products marks a concrete step in advancing pension finance and will offer investors a wider range of options and bring more long-term capital into the capital market, China Securities Journal reported, citing industry insiders. (China Securities Journal)

Some veteran Chinese asset managers are freezing subscriptions to their funds, an indication that stocks are too expensive now after a blistering run. (SCMP)

UK-based cross-border payment firm Ebury is looking to ramp up hiring in China, driven by local companies expanding trade overseas and the increasing use of the yuan in global commerce. (BBG)

BoJ minutes from the September meeting showed a growing number of policymakers who believed that conditions were falling into place for interest rates to rise, with two members advocating an immediate increase. (RTRS)

Japan's military deployed troops to the country's mountainous north on Wednesday to help trap bears after an urgent request from local authorities struggling to cope with a wave of attacks. (RTRS)

British money managers are reporting a jump in people withdrawing cash from their pensions before this month's budget, amid fears for their tax advantages as the government warns it needs to make "hard choices" to prop up public finances. (RTRS)

The Office for Budget Responsibility, whose forecasts underpin UK budgets, is poised to hand Labour’s Reeves a hit of as much as £20 billion by lowering its estimates for UK productivity by 0.3 percentage points. (BBG)

UK Chancellor Reeves needs to embark on major tax rises in her November 26 budget or risk a repeat of the loss of market confidence that cost former prime minister Liz Truss her job, The National Institute of Economic and Social Research has said, a leading think-tank, calling on Reeves to build 30 billion pounds of margin for error against economic shocks, up from 10 billion at her last budget. (RTRS)

UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves will meet CEOs from top insurers in Downing Street on Wednesday, as she seeks to encourage more investment in the City ahead of a tricky budget later this month. (BBG)

Pay settlements awarded by British employers held steady in the three months to September, according to a survey published a day before the Bank of England's interest rates decision. Incomes Data Research said that the median pay rise awarded by major employers was 3% in the July to September period, holding at the joint lowest level since December 2021. (RTRS)

German manufacturing orders and industrial production in France rebounded in September, signaling a recovery in the factory sector after trade uncertainty dented demand over the summer. (WSJ)

The issuance of Kangaroo bonds has jumped nearly 60% this year as global companies diversify away from markets denominated in U.S. dollars, a trend that is expected to continue into 2026, Westpac said on Tuesday. (RTRS)

New Zealand's jobless rate rose to 5.3% in the third quarter, its highest level since 2016, as employment remained unchanged, according to data released by Statistics New Zealand on Wednesday. Kiwi hits seven-month low after weak jobs data. (RTRS)

Russia and Turkey are in talks to keep up the volumes of gas supplies from Gazprom PJSC as they negotiate the renewal of two major pipeline supply deals, according to Bloomberg sources. (BBG)

Argentine President Javier Milei and his Economy Minister Luis Caputo will meet a select group of investors and company representatives in New York this week, according to Bloomberg sources. (BBG)

GEOPOLITICAL:

Taiwan has revoked the citizenship of 50 individuals who also held mainland Chinese passports and household registrations, citing the need to curb infiltration. (SCMP)

North Korea is preparing for a potential summit meeting between leader Kim Jong Un and President Donald Trump as the idea was broached during Trump’s recent visit to Asia, based on an assessment by South Korea’s National Intelligence Service. (BBG)

EQUITIES:

Advanced Micro Devices failed to impress investors with its revenue forecast, despite it sitting comfortably above analyst forecasts, after an eye-popping rally sent expectations soaring. (BBG)

Super Micro Computer Inc. shares tumbled in late trading after the server maker missed reduced estimates for first-quarter sales and profit and gave a disappointing earnings forecast for the current period, reinforcing concerns about its ability to capitalize on demand for AI equipment. (BBG)

Deutsche Bank is exploring ways to hedge its exposure to data centres after extending billions of dollars in debt to the sector. The German lender is looking at options including shorting a basket of AI-related stocks that would help mitigate downside risk by betting against companies in the sector. It is also considering buying default protection on some of the debt using derivatives through a transaction known as synthetic risk transfer (SRT). (FT)

Coupang Inc. slid in late trading after reporting third-quarter profits that fell far short of Wall Street’s projections in the face of heightened competition. (BBG)

Alphabet Inc.’s Google and cybersecurity company Wiz Inc. cleared a key hurdle to closing their $32 billion deal, with the US government saying it would wrap up its investigation of the acquisition. (BBG)

Cava Group Inc. cut its full-year sales growth targets after foot traffic stalled in the third quarter, adding to worrying trends that financially squeezed consumers are forgoing fast-casual restaurants. (BBG)

Rivian Automotive Inc. reported a smaller-than-expected loss in a sign of progress as the electric-vehicle maker cuts costs and staff ahead of plans to begin deliveries of a new midsize SUV next year. (BBG)

Pinterest Inc. projected revenue for the current quarter that fell short of analysts’ estimates, a sign that the search platform’s advertising business may not be growing as quickly as expected despite the upcoming holiday shopping season. The stock plunged more than 19% in after-hours trading. (BBG)

Match Group Inc. provided a weaker-than-expected fourth-quarter revenue outlook and warned that product testing at its largest dating app, Tinder, will come at the expense of short-term gains. (BBG)

American International Group Inc.’s third-quarter profit beat Wall Street’s expectations, increasing year-over-year despite losses from its separation of Corebridge Financial Inc. (BBG)

Australia broadened its social media ban for under-16s to include some second-tier platforms including Reddit, a little more than a month before the world-first legislation takes effect. (BBG)

The scientist who oversaw development of Tencent Holdings Ltd.’s flagship AI model has raised $50 million with a startup planning to release a rival to OpenAI’s Sora, the latest high-profile entry in one of the more profitable of artificial intelligence spheres. (BBG)

Country Garden Holdings Co., one of the biggest casualties of China’s real estate crisis, is wrapping up its $14.1 billion offshore debt restructuring after more than two years, with creditors likely to approve its plan in a vote on Wednesday. (BBG)

Taiwan’s cabinet instructed the Ministry of Digital Affairs, the Ministry of Finance, and the Ministry of Transportation to study strengthening management of offshore e-commerce platforms, according to a statement from the island’s Ministry of Economic Affairs. (BBG)

Toyota raised its full-year profit forecast on Wednesday, with the Japanese automaker betting that cost-cutting and strong demand for hybrids would help it ride out the impact of U.S. President Donald Trump's tariffs. (RTRS)

Nissan Motor will cut production of its top-selling Rogue SUV in Japan from next week due to a short supply of chips from Dutch firm Nexperia, according to a Reuters sources, the latest fallout from the diplomatic turmoil involving the chipmaker. (RTRS)

Hong Kong Exchanges & Clearing reported record profit and revenue for the third quarter as trading and listing activity in the Asian financial hub gathered momentum. (WSJ)

BMW AG’s profit margin came in toward the lower end of its guidance in the third quarter as tariffs and intense competition in China cut into earnings. (BBG)

Siemens Healthineers SHL -9.18%decrease; red down pointing triangle reported a fall in fourth-quarter profit after higher comparable revenue stemming from the restructuring of its diagnostics business was offset by a hit from U.S. tariffs. (WSJ)

Barratt Redrow, Britain's largest homebuilder, said on Wednesday bookings slowed during the June 30-October 26 period, as mounting economic uncertainties kept potential buyers on the sidelines. (RTRS)

Marks & Spencer reported a 55.4% slide in first-half underlying profit, reflecting the impact on sales and margins of an April cyber hack that forced it to suspend online clothing orders for seven weeks and also hit food availability. Co. expects profit in the second half of the year to rebound. (RTRS/BBG)

UK Pub chain JD Wetherspoon on Wednesday projected a more cautious outlook for the rest of the year ahead of the upcoming UK budget, and posted a slowdown in sales growth due to a squeeze in consumer spending. (RTRS)

Magnum Ice Cream is targeting Dec. 8 for its initial public offering, after the spinoff of Unilever’s ice-cream business pushed back its listing and said the U.S. government shutdown was to blame. (WSJ)

Novo Nordisk lowered its full-year profit forecast on Wednesday in an early blow to the Danish drugmaker's new CEO amid a deep restructuring drive to claw back lost ground in a fierce obesity drug market battle. (RTRS)

Orsted A/S confirmed its full-year profit guidance, seeking to reassure investors of its financial stability after setbacks in the US forced the offshore wind developer to raise more than $9 billion from shareholders. (BBG)

Vestas Wind Systems VWS 12.55%increase; green up pointing triangle said third-quarter net profit rose as it benefited from higher deliveries and an improved performance at its onshore unit. (WSJ)

#MSNews | The Philippine Air Force (PAF), in coordination with the Philippine Army and local authorities, has completed the retrieval of the remains of six (6) aircrew members from the Super Huey helicopter that crashed in Agusan del Sur on November 4, 2025.

The aircraft was on a humanitarian assistance and disaster response (HADR) mission in the aftermath of Tropical Storm Tino when the accident occurred. An investigation is ongoing to determine the cause of the crash.

The PAF expresses its deepest condolences to the families and loved ones of the fallen heroes. 

"Their dedication, courage, and selfless service in the performance of duty embody the highest ideals of the organization and will forever be remembered with honor." PAF Spokesperson Col. Ma. Christina Basco said. | via Rex Espiritu

📷 PAF

【台風被害情報】
台風25号（カルマエギ）がフィリピン中部を直撃。観光地セブ島で洪水・家屋倒壊など甚大な被害。死者90人超、行方不明者多数。空軍ヘリ墜落で6人死亡。都市部が浸水し停電・断水が続く。台風は勢力を保ちベトナム方面へ。
#台風25号 #フィリピン #セブ島 #災害情報

📍詳細
［人的被害］
・死者：90人超（うちセブ州で76人）
・行方不明者：26人以上
・負傷者：多数（洪水・倒壊・感電など）
［物的被害］
・家屋損壊・流出：多数（沿岸・低地中心）
・車両流出・がれき堆積：都市道路が川のように冠水
・停電・断水：広範囲で発生、通信障害も継続
［インフラ被害］
・橋梁・道路の寸断、避難所へ通行困難
・空軍ヘリ1機墜落（救援中、乗員6人死亡）
・空港・港湾の運航停止、数千人が避難
［気象状況］
・24時間雨量：セブ市で最大183mm（月平均超）
・最大瞬間風速：毎秒46m
・今後、台風は西進しベトナムへ接近見込み。

🌪️BREAKING: Typhoon #Kalmaegi (No.25) slammed the central Philippines, devastating Cebu Island with floods and collapsed homes. Over 90 dead, dozens missing. A military rescue helicopter crashed, killing 6. Power and water outages continue as the storm heads toward Vietnam. #Philippines #Cebu

📍Details (Damage Summary)
[Casualties]
• Over 90 confirmed dead (76 in Cebu Province)
• At least 26 missing, many injured by floods and debris
[Property Damage]
• Widespread flooding swept away vehicles and homes
• Urban roads turned into rivers, massive debris accumulation
• Power and water outages, telecommunication disruptions
[Infrastructure]
• Roads and bridges cut off, isolating some communities
• Air Force helicopter crashed during relief mission—6 dead
• Airports and ports suspended operations; thousands evacuated
[Weather Conditions]
• 24-hour rainfall reached 183 mm in Cebu City (exceeding monthly average)
• Peak wind gusts: 46 m/s
• Typhoon continues westward, forecast to approach Vietnam on Nov 6
#TyphoonKalmaegi #Philippines #Cebu #DisasterResponse #Floods
